subject: Next steps: Medexa trial deployment & success gates
messages:

Subject: Next steps: Medexa trial deployment & success gates

Hi Ava —

Great talking earlier. Quick recap from our call and a recommended path for the trial so we can lock timelines and owners:  

High-level success criteria (what Medexa wants to validate):
- Inference latency: median response time < 250ms for 1–2k concurrent short-text requests
- Cost target: amortized inference cost per 1k tokens under the threshold you shared (approx $0.85)
- Security posture: environment meets PHI handling controls (audit logs, KMS, VPC isolation)
- Integration: sample API calls + auth scheme exercised by your devs and one end-to-end workflow with live dataset

Environment options we discussed (tradeoffs):
1) Hosted Redwood API (fastest): minimal setup, lowest time-to-first-query. Good for early functional validation but not suitable if you need network isolation or specific KMS.
2) Dedicated sandbox (reserved GPUs, isolated tenant): predictable throughput and can be configured with restricted data retention. Short setup (2–3 business days) if we reuse standard image.
3) Private VPC deployment (recommended given PHI): customer VPC peering or private link + KMS/HSM. Longer lead time (3–4 weeks) due to networking and security approvals.

Proposed immediate plan (mutual action plan):
- Week 1 (Oct 2–6): Confirm environment choice + legal procurement kickoff (Medexa).
- Week 2 (Oct 9–13): Provision environment (hosted sandbox or dedicated). If VPC chosen, begin networking scoping and security questionnaire.
- Week 3 (Oct 16–20): Integration window — API keys, sample dataset ingest, run baseline evals. 
- Week 4 (Oct 23–27): Run acceptance tests against success criteria; review results and decide go/no-go for extended pilot.

Asks for Medexa from this thread:
- Preferred environment (hosted / dedicated sandbox / VPC). If VPC, who is your network lead so we can kick off peering?
- Legal / procurement contact we should loop in for PO and contract redlines.
- Two sample queries (anonymized) and expected outputs so we can prepare an acceptance test.

I attached a PO template and a starter success-criteria spreadsheet to save you time. Camila (solutions) and Karthik (trial ops) are cc'd to scope infra and performance targets. If you confirm VPC, we will schedule a short tech scoping call with your network/security team.

Thanks — I can be available Tue/Thu mornings next week to sync.

— Marcus Lin

Hi Ava —

Thanks for confirming the preference for VPC. Quick notes from an infra/solutions standpoint and a recommended technical onramp:  

VPC checklist (what we need to scope):
- Network peering method: AWS VPC peering or PrivateLink? Which does Raj prefer?
- CIDR ranges and proposed NAT/egress requirements.
- KMS approach: we support customer-managed CMKs via AWS KMS. HSM integrations can be scoped as an add-on; let us know if you require FIPS 140-2 certs.
- Audit logs: We can deliver audit logging to your S3 bucket (encrypted) with retention policy configurable; default 90 days, extendable to 365 days for enterprise plans.

Performance baseline for dedicated/private setups (typical):
- 1x p4d-equivalent node baseline yields ~800–1200 short-text QPS with median latency ~180–260ms depending on prompt length. We’ll instrument real traffic during the integration window and tune batching/cache settings.

Mutual action plan (tech owner assignments):
- Medexa: Raj Patel — network configuration, firewall approvals, provide CIDR + peering contact.
- Redwood: Camila Reyes — tech provisioning, network fingerprint, onboarding runbook.
- Redwood ops: Karthik Iyer — API keys, quota config, and acceptance test harness.

I attached a lightweight acceptance-test template (sheet in the drive link Marcus shared) and a short checklist for the VPC kick-off. Suggest a 30–45m tech scoping call this week with Raj + Karthik.

Camila Reyes
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

5) Procurement/legal: procurement@medexa.com / legal@medexa.com — please confirm the person who will own the PO and the contract. We've attached our PO template; feel free to return a redlined contract.
